_comment: Real plants, with an append-only status history. This is the file the watch agent's
second channel writes to, and the reason its shape is strict.
Schema and vocabularies: sources/sector_map.py. Gate: sources/check_sector_schema.py.
STATUS_HISTORY IS APPEND-ONLY AND EVERY ENTRY CARRIES A SOURCE. A status that changed
without a link is a status nobody can check, and the history is the one part of this
layer that is meant to be read as a record rather than as an analysis. Entries are in
date order and the last one equals `status`; the gate fails on either being untrue,
because a header and a timeline that disagree put two different facts on one page.
A SHORT HISTORY IS HONEST. Several of these projects start their history at the event
this repository first sourced — the grant, the groundbreaking — rather than at their
announcement, because no primary source for the earlier event has been read yet. The
file records what was verified, not what is likely to have happened.
`public_funding.measure` points at the register measure that IS the programme, and carries
`measure_note` saying how tight the fit is. The Innovation Fund lines are the live case: the
grants were awarded under the Fund as it stands (Art. 10a(8) of the ETS Directive), while the
register knows the Fund through the revision's Art. 10cb, which re-establishes it. Linking them
is what lets the money model total public support for the sector; the note is what stops the
link from being read as a claim that the award was made under the proposed article.

`public_funding` used to sit on each row. It moved to data/transition/funding.json, where capital allocation is a node with edges out of it: one Innovation Fund call finances several projects, and a field on the recipient could only say so by repeating itself once per recipient. The project keeps a rollup and the rollup is DERIVED — computed from the funding rows wherever it is shown, never stored back here.
`shared`: OPTIONAL, AND ONLY EVER TRUE. A project is claimed by the ecosystem whose
product it makes (page specifications §4.2), and two claims on one project fail the
build — a boundary drawn twice is a boundary somebody has to redraw. A CO2 store or a
hydrogen pipeline serving three industries is the exception the rule needs, and it
says so with "shared": true and a note giving the industries it serves. A plant making
one product never carries it.
WHERE IT IS, IN THE SAME BREATH AS WHAT IT IS. `location` is a LIST of sites, because a
project is not always at one place: the ArcelorMittal row covers Bremen and
Eisenhüttenstadt, and a single point for it would put a fact on the map that is half
wrong. One site is the ordinary case and the list of one says so honestly.
Every site carries {site, lat, lon, precision, retrieved_date, source, confidence} — the
parameter discipline, applied to a coordinate. `precision` is `plant` for a works and
`site` for a store or a terminal; `town` is in the vocabulary only so that the gate can
name what it is refusing. A town centroid is not a plant location: it would draw a mark
a reader would take for the works, several kilometres from the works. The coordinates
are read off OpenStreetMap features that carry the operator's or the works' own name,
which is a source that states a position rather than an address somebody geocoded in
their head; where a company publishes the plant address, `address` records it beside the
point. `confidence` is `secondary` throughout: OpenStreetMap is a third party reporting
somebody else's site.
`role` says what kind of place it is, and the map draws each differently. `plant` is the
default and is omitted; `storage` is a permitted or proposed geological store. A store is
in this file rather than in one of its own because it is what this file already says it
is — a real installation with an append-only status history — and because the exception
the `shared` flag was written for is exactly a CO2 store serving several industries.
`storage` IS REQUIRED ON EVERY CAPTURE PROJECT and has two shapes. Either it names the
project id of the store the tonne reaches, with the source that names it; or it says
`"unresolved": true` with a note saying how far the chain is actually specified. Five of
the nine capture projects here are unresolved, and that is the finding, not a hole: a
kiln with a capture unit and nowhere to send the CO2 is the thing the sector page exists
to show. An unresolved row still carries a source, because "nobody has said" is itself a
claim about a document somebody read.

sources.note:
PRODUCT SCOPE AT PERMIT TIER, and it settles the product rule on this row: the report walks the Electrode Area, then 'Area A – Cell Assembly', 'Area B – Cell Processing' and 'Area C – Module Production'. Electrodes are made and cells are assembled on site, so it is a cell works and the module line is downstream of that rather than instead of it.

NAMING AND CAPACITY DISAGREE ACROSS THE TWO SOURCES, and the disagreement is carried rather than resolved. This report, issued 26 September 2023, is titled for the 'Giga 1 Car Battery Manufacturing Facility' and consents a maximum of up to 9 GWh per annum 'split across two battery manufacturing plants separated by a central spine of offices'. AESC's launch release of December 2025 calls the works 'Plant 2' at 15.8 GWh. A permit states a consented maximum at its filing date and a launch release states what was built, so the capacities need not agree. The naming does not follow from that — though the permit's own phrase, two manufacturing plants inside one Giga 1 installation, is the likeliest explanation and is not stated anywhere read so far, so it stays an observation and not a finding.

source.note: THE PERMIT IS THE SOURCE OF THE POSITION AND NO BASEMAP FEATURE IS. The integrated environmental authorisation of 17 May 2023 for Envision AESC Spain SL states the installation's representative coordinates and names the cadastral parcel — 'parcela catastral I-67' — on a plot of 1 088 211 m². The stored latitude and longitude are RECOMPUTED from the easting and northing by sources/utm.py on every build, so the conversion cannot be done once by hand and quietly adjusted. Corroboration and not placement: the point falls 152 m outside the mapped edge of the 'Expacio Navalmoral' industrial estate, which is the park the permit names and whose polygon covers what was already built there — an estate is refused as a position on this platform, so it stands here as a check on the arithmetic rather than as the source.

projects.capacity_note: The permit's figure for the END OF PHASE FOUR — 'la capacidad total de fabricación de baterías, al final de la cuarta etapa en 2028, sea de 94,24 GWh al año' — and not what the first phase builds. AESC's own release states no GWh at all, so this is a permit-tier capacity for a four-phase build whose first phase is what is under construction.

status_history.note: AESC's own first-stone release: 'Today, Monday, July 8, marked the groundbreaking ceremony of AESC's future gigafactory for batteries in Navalmoral de la Mata, Cáceres.' La Moncloa and the Junta de Extremadura record the same ceremony, with the Prime Minister and the President of the Junta present. TWO TIMETABLES THAT DO NOT AGREE, AND BOTH ARE HELD. The 2024 release says the plant 'is scheduled to begin production in 2026'; the Junta told the Extremadura Assembly in June 2026 that construction concludes in November 2027 and the first cells come in December 2028, and an opposition deputy in the same session said that two years after the first stone there is 'la primera piedra y nada más'. The status is what none of them disputes — ground was broken and no cell has been made — and the four-and-a-half-year gap between the ceremony and the first cell is the fact a reader should have, not a discrepancy to be resolved by taking the newest number silently.

projects.name: SVOLT Überherrn

source.note: THE PLAN NAMES THE PARCELS AND THE STATE CADASTRE HOLDS THEIR GEOMETRY, and the point is the area-weighted centroid of the two put together — the same construction as Sunderland's, where the permit listed emission points and the centroid of those was the works. 57 of the 58 parcels the Begründung lists as wholly inside the Geltungsbereich were found in Gemarkung Überherrn, Flur 1 and Flur 3, in the Saarland INSPIRE cadastral service (LVGL, dl-de/by-2-0); 152/11 was not, and four labels occur in both Fluren and are both counted, which moves the point by tens of metres. They total 77.1 ha against the plan's stated 99, the balance being the road and watercourse parcels the same page lists as only partly inside. THE PLAN AREA IS NOT THE WORKS: the factory footprint inside it was about 52 ha, and nothing was ever built, so the precision is `site` and the point is the centre of the area the plan covered rather than of a building.

projects.capacity_note: The company's figure for the final expansion stage, from its own EU-Locations page: 'a battery cell factory with 24 GWh of installed capacity in the final expansion stage is to be built'. No stage of it was built.

status_history.note: SVOLT's own EU-Locations page, as the Internet Archive captured it on 24 July 2024: 'In Überherrn on "Linslerfeld", a battery cell factory with 24 GWh of installed capacity in the final expansion stage is to be built.' The site was announced in 2020 and this is the earliest company statement about it that this pipeline has read; the capture date is what the row can defend, not the announcement date.

THE CANCELLATION IS THE AUTHORITY'S OWN, not press. The Überherrn council resolved on 7 May 2026 to repeal the plan, and the notice says why: 'Gegenstand der Aufhebung ist der Vorhabenbezogene Bebauungsplan „Industriegebiet Linsler Feld“, der die planungsrechtlichen Voraussetzungen für die Ansiedlung einer Batteriezellfabrik schaffen sollte. Das Vorhaben wird nicht mehr umgesetzt.' The repeal Begründung records the mechanism: gwSaar, the Vorhabenträger that had bought the land to grant SVOLT a heritable building right, declared it would not hold to the project, which triggers the municipality's duty to repeal under § 12 Abs. 6 BauGB. SVOLT's European withdrawal was reported earlier in trade press and no company statement of it has been read here, so the date this row carries is the authority's.
